candidates.author: G. K. Chesterton
candidates.sourceEdition: The Man Who Was Thursday: A Nightmare, J. W. Arrowsmith, Bristol, with London distribution by Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co., 1908
candidates.notes: Project Gutenberg eBook #1695 is the complete-text candidate and identifies the work as public domain in the USA. The 1908 original scan is identified by Wikimedia Commons as a 340-page file from the Internet Archive, published by J. W. Arrowsmith and Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co.; author death is recorded as 14 June 1936. The Intellectual Property Office of Ireland states literary copyright expires 70 years after the author's death and typographical arrangement of a published edition after 50 years; this supports a preliminary calculation of the underlying text entering the Irish public domain on 1 January 2007 and the 1908 edition layout term expiring after 1958. This is a preliminary source-based calculation, not legal sign-off; edition-specific additions and territorial exceptions still require review. Gutenberg HTML confirms chapter I and the ending marker; sampled chapter headings include I, IV, X and XIV, but a full page-by-page comparison of the Gutenberg text against the original scan remains outstanding. The Wikisource transcription is CC BY-SA and must not be copied into CICAN without meeting its attribution/share-alike terms. A named human transcription reviewer remains outstanding. Do not publish until all gates pass.

candidates.author: John Buchan
candidates.sourceEdition: The Thirty-Nine Steps, William Blackwood and Sons, Edinburgh and London, 1915, first book edition (reported publication date 19 October 1915)
candidates.notes: Project Gutenberg eBook #558 supplies a complete English text candidate and explicitly marks it public domain in the USA; its HTML exposes ten chapter headings and the September 1915 dedication. The National Library of Scotland confirms serialisation in Blackwood's Magazine in July–September 1915 and book publication by William Blackwood and Sons, Edinburgh and London, in October 1915. A Google Books record linked from the 'Other editions' list is marked Full view - 1915 and exposes PDF, EPUB and plain-text download controls; its record ID is S0pAO7s-TkEC. The PDF download request returned HTTP 403 through this research interface, so scan pages have not yet been obtained or collated. Ravn Forlag's 2026 edition states its text was read page by page against a Google-digitised scan of the first edition, preserving wording, British spelling, chapter titles and dedication but correcting and documenting obvious misprints; this is useful corroboration, not a reusable transcription because its 2026 editorial contributions are separately protected. A rare-book dealer independently describes a 1915 first edition, William Blackwood and Sons, with pagination [9], 10–253, [3]. John Buchan (1875–1940) supports a preliminary Irish life-plus-70 calculation of 1 January 2011 under IPOI guidance; Gutenberg explicitly marks US public-domain status. These are preliminary source-based findings, not legal sign-off. Exact scan-page acquisition and independent page-by-page comparison of the Gutenberg text, review of any edition-specific elements, and named human transcription review remain outstanding. Do not publish until all gates pass.

candidates.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
candidates.sourceEdition: The Lost World: Being an Account of the Recent Amazing Adventures of Professor George E. Challenger..., Hodder & Stoughton, London, 15 October 1912, first edition in book form
candidates.notes: Project Gutenberg eBook #139 provides a complete English text candidate and explicitly identifies it as public domain in the USA. Google Books identifies a Harvard University digitisation of The Lost World, Hodder & Stoughton, 1912, 309 pages; its contents list all 16 chapters, but this Google Books record currently presents snippet view rather than a page-readable full scan. Open Library identifies a 1912 Hodder & Stoughton edition with 319 pages and eight leaves of plates, linked to Internet Archive item lostworld0000sira_n3v3; other catalogue records identify lostworld01doylgoog and lostworld00doyluoft as 1912 digitised copies, but the exact imprint/issue and image completeness must be confirmed from title-page and collation evidence before using them as the first UK book edition. Peter Harrington's bibliographical catalogue describes the first edition in book form as London, Hodder and Stoughton, [1912], with frontispiece and seven plates; an ABAA catalogue gives 319, [1] imprint pages and plates. Pagination and plate counts differ between catalogue records, so this is not yet a settled edition identification. The novel was serialised in The Strand and Philadelphia Press before book publication; Oxford University Press notes textual variants between serial and first book edition, so Gutenberg must be compared against the exact first book edition, not the serial. Doyle died 7 July 1930; under IPOI life-plus-70 guidance this supports a preliminary Irish public-domain date of 1 January 2001 for the underlying text, while the 1912 typographical arrangement term appears to have expired after 1962. Gutenberg explicitly states US public-domain status. This is a preliminary source-based calculation, not legal sign-off. Any illustrations require separate rights review; text-only is the intended route unless image rights are independently cleared. No page-by-page collation or named human transcription review has been completed. Do not publish until exact-edition collation, Ireland/US rights review and all human attestations pass. Additional high-value scan candidate located: Internet Archive identifier lostworldbeingac00doylrich, digitised by the California Digital Library and mirrored on Wikimedia Commons as a 344-page, 16.07 MB PDF. The scan metadata gives title, author Arthur Conan Doyle (1859–1930), London/New York, Hodder and Stoughton, publication date [1912], and links directly to the IA PDF. This is materially closer to the target first UK edition than the earlier generic Google Books references, but Commons categorises the scan under an unverified-scan category; title-page, edition statement, collation, illustrations and all text pages must be checked before accepting it as the definitive 1912 first-edition witness. The PDF timed out through the web reader and direct download failed in this session; no page-level comparison has been performed. The Google Books Harvard record separately confirms a 1912 Hodder & Stoughton digitisation with 309 catalogue pages, while first-edition bookseller catalogues describe the UK first edition as 319 pages plus imprint and eight illustrations/plates; catalogue pagination differences likely reflect front matter and scanning conventions and must be reconciled, not assumed away. Source-quality clarification from the Commons file record: the PDF is 344 scanned pages (file 16.07 MiB; Commons preview says 7.05 MB), and its bibliographic description names London/New York, Hodder and Stoughton, [1912], OCLC 263174507, and IA identifier lostworldbeingac00doylrich. The Commons structured inception field says 1894, which conflicts with the record's own title, publisher, and 1912 bibliographic sources and appears to be unreliable metadata; do not treat 1894 as the edition date. The scan is hosted under a public-domain label for the US pre-1931 publication rule, but this label does not replace Irish rights analysis. The Oxford edition's note explicitly states the 1912 first book edition replaced some serial illustrations and contains numerous textual variants from the serial, mainly punctuation in the final chapters; it gives three examples of wording/punctuation differences between the Strand text and the first book edition. This reinforces the need to collate against the 1912 book scan. The scan PDF link is recorded, but actual page-level inspection and full comparison remain outstanding.
